skills.name: research (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/research/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Delegate a question to a background agent that investigates it against primary sources and captures findings in the repo.
skills.mechanism: Spawns a background agent so the main session keeps working; hard rules: primary sources only (follow every claim to the source that owns it), one Markdown file with per-claim citations, saved where the repo already keeps such notes (match convention or state the chosen location).

skills.name: wizard (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/wizard/SKILL.md + template.sh)
skills.purpose: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human step-by-step through a procedure only they can perform (credentials, dashboards, migrations).
skills.mechanism: A frozen 204-line library (never hand-edit) supplies UX primitives — stage/progress display, screen-clearing per stage, confirm gates before irreversible actions, hidden secret entry, idempotent .env upserts, resumable re-runs; the agent only scopes stages from repo evidence (.env.example, CI secrets.*), maps each stage to concrete click-paths (never inventing UI steps), authors stages, and verifies statically (bash -n, shellcheck, trace values) without running it.

skills.name: handoff (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/handoff/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document a fresh agent can pick up.
skills.mechanism: Writes to the OS temp dir (not the workspace); includes a 'suggested skills' section routing the next agent; references existing artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, commits) by path instead of duplicating them; redacts secrets/PII; an optional argument tailors the doc to the next session's focus.
skills.invocation: user-typed only (disable-model-invocation: true; openai.yaml allow_implicit_invocation: false)

skills.name: prototype (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/prototype/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Build throwaway code that answers exactly one design question.
skills.mechanism: Router: branches by question type — 'does this logic feel right?' → LOGIC.md, 'what should this look like?' → UI.md — with shared hard rules: clearly marked throwaway, trivial to run, no persistence, no polish, full state surfaced after every action, and on completion the answer is folded into real code while the prototype is preserved as a primary source on a throwaway branch with a pointer from the issue.

skills.name: prototype/LOGIC.md (reference branch)
skills.purpose: Answer a state-model/business-logic question with a single shareable HTML demo a non-developer can drive.
skills.mechanism: Question stated visibly at the top; the logic lives in one pure, liftable module (reducer/state machine/pure functions) with the page as a thin shell; layout is fixed: current-state panel, free-play buttons, and tabbed guided walkthrough scenarios (reset to known state) targeting edge cases; all labels in domain language.

skills.name: prototype/UI.md (reference branch)
skills.purpose: Answer 'what should this look like?' by generating 3-5 radically different UI variants switchable in the browser.
skills.mechanism: Variants mount on an existing route (preferred) gated by ?variant= URL param with a floating arrow-key switcher bar hidden in production; variants must be structurally different (redo any two that converge); winner is folded in, losers and switcher move to the throwaway branch.

skills.name: domain-modeling (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md + CONTEXT-FORMAT.md + ADR-FORMAT.md)
skills.purpose: Actively build and sharpen the project's glossary (CONTEXT.md) and decision records (ADRs) during design conversations.
skills.mechanism: In-session disciplines: challenge terms that conflict with the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language into canonical terms with _Avoid_ synonym lists, stress-test relationships with invented edge-case scenarios, cross-check user claims against the code, and update CONTEXT.md inline the moment a term resolves (never batch); files created lazily; ADRs are one-paragraph records offered only when a three-part gate passes (hard to reverse AND surprising without context AND a real trade-off).

skills.name: codebase-design (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md + DEEPENING.md + DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md)
skills.purpose: Shared controlled vocabulary and principles for designing deep modules (much behavior behind a small interface).
skills.mechanism: An enforced glossary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) with explicit banned synonyms and a 'rejected framings' section; principles as tests (deletion test, interface-is-the-test-surface, one adapter = hypothetical seam); DEEPENING.md classifies dependencies into four categories that dictate test strategy; DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md spawns 3+ parallel subagents each under a different design constraint, presents designs sequentially, compares on named axes, and ends with an opinionated recommendation or hybrid.
skills.invocation: model-invoked; also serves as shared reference other skills call

skills.name: writing-for-agents (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md + SKILL-MECHANICS.md)
skills.purpose: Reference for writing any document an agent consumes so the agent takes the same process every run.
skills.mechanism: A theory of harness authoring: context pointers whose wording decides trigger reliability; two budgets (context load on the agent vs cognitive load on the human); an information hierarchy with progressive disclosure behind pointers; completion criteria graded on clarity and demand; 'leading words' that recruit pretrained priors; prefer positive phrasing over negation; pruning tests (single source of truth, environment-as-truth, no-op detection); SKILL-MECHANICS.md covers the model-invoked vs user-invoked trade and router skills.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md + HTML-REPORT.md)
skills.purpose: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them visually, then interactively work through the chosen one.
skills.mechanism: Three-phase pipeline with a hard stop: (1) scope via git-history hot spots then subagent exploration guided by friction questions and the deletion test; (2) self-contained HTML report (Tailwind+Mermaid CDN) in the temp dir with per-candidate cards — before/after diagrams, wins in glossary terms only, Strong/Worth-exploring/Speculative badges, ADR-conflict callouts — and no interface proposals until the user picks; (3) a grilling loop with inline side effects (CONTEXT.md updates, rejection-reason ADRs, design-it-twice on demand).

skills.name: resolving-merge-conflicts (/home/eranr/.agents/skills/resolving-merge-conflicts/SKILL.md)
skills.purpose: Resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict faithfully to both sides' intent.
skills.mechanism: Five-step checklist: see current state; trace each conflict to its primary sources (commit messages, PRs, original issues) to recover intent; resolve preserving both intents where possible with hard rules (never invent behavior, never --abort); run the project's automated checks; finish the merge/rebase.

patterns: Background delegation with a durable artifact as the only output: the delegated agent's product is a cited file placed by existing repo convention, not a chat reply.

Frozen library + authored-stages template for human-in-loop procedures: the agent authors only the variable part, and the invariant UX/safety layer (confirm gates, resumability, secret handling) is identical across every generated instance and never edited.
Static verification of interactive artifacts: never run the human-facing procedure end-to-end; trace it on paper against the scoped value list instead.
Multi-criterion gates before creating durable records: an ADR is offered only when hard-to-reverse AND surprising AND a real trade-off all hold, keeping the archive high-signal.
Lazy file creation: glossaries and decision folders are created only when the first real entry exists, never as empty scaffolding.
Enforced controlled vocabulary with banned synonyms and documented rejected framings, propagated into every downstream artifact and subagent brief.

Question-first throwaway artifacts: state the question visibly at the top, branch the artifact's shape on the question type, and on completion capture both the verdict and the artifact as a primary source off the mainline.
Design-it-twice via parallel subagents with orthogonal constraints (minimal / flexible / common-case), sequential presentation, comparison on named axes, and a mandatory opinionated recommendation.
Hard stop between survey and commitment: generate the candidate report, ask the human to pick, and explicitly forbid proposing solutions before the pick.
Handoff compaction rules: reference existing artifacts by path instead of duplicating, include a suggested-skills routing section, redact secrets, write outside the workspace.
Invocation policy as a design lever: model-invoked skills pay permanent context load for discoverability, user-typed-only skills pay human cognitive load, and router skills consolidate the latter.
Inline capture discipline: update the glossary or decision log the moment a term or decision crystallizes — never batch to the end of the session.
Primary-source tracing as the universal epistemic rule: every claim, conflict hunk, or wizard step is followed back to the source that owns it, and unknown steps are asked about rather than invented.
Self-contained visual HTML reports in the temp dir with a fixed card grammar (problem/solution/wins/badge/before-after diagram) and a graded recommendation-strength taxonomy.

Completion-criterion engineering: word each step's done-condition to be checkable and demanding ('every modified model accounted for'), and hide later steps across a context boundary when they tempt rushing.
Progressive disclosure: keep the top-level skill short and push branch-specific reference into sibling files reached only when that branch fires.
knowledgeWorkAnalogs: Research capture: a background agent that answers a question from primary sources (papers, official docs, datasets) and files a literature note with per-claim citations into the vault following its existing note conventions.

Wizard for human-only knowledge chores: a generated interactive checklist that walks the human through portals only they can drive (journal submission, IRB forms, archive access requests, grant systems), capturing IDs and confirmation numbers into a project metadata file, resumable and gated before irreversible submissions.

Session handoff notes: compact a long research/writing conversation into a temp-dir handoff that references existing notes and drafts by link instead of restating them, names which skills the next session should invoke, and is tailored to the stated next focus.

Argument prototypes: a single shareable HTML walkthrough that lets a colleague or domain expert push a conceptual model/framework through edge-case scenarios via buttons — surfacing 'wait, that shouldn't follow' bugs in the idea before the paper is written.

Outline-it-thrice: generate 3-5 structurally different outlines of the same essay/report (chronological vs thematic vs problem-first), flip between them side by side, keep the winner and archive the rest with the verdict recorded.

Project glossary discipline: a live CONTEXT.md for a research project's terminology with canonical terms and _Avoid_ synonym lists, challenged and updated inline during discussion, plus one-paragraph decision records for methodology choices (corpus exclusions, coding schemes) gated by hard-to-reverse/surprising/real-trade-off.

Deep-note vocabulary for PKM: a controlled vocabulary for vault architecture (a 'deep' index note = many sources behind a small entry point; the deletion test = would removing this hub scatter its links across N notes?) enforced across restructuring work.

Vault architecture audit: scan a note collection's edit-history hot spots for structural friction, present restructuring candidates as a visual HTML report with before/after link diagrams and Strong/Worth-exploring/Speculative badges, stop for the human's pick, then work through the chosen restructuring while updating the glossary inline.

Draft reconciliation: merge divergent versions of a document or contradictory sources by tracing each conflict back to its origin and intent, preserving both intents where compatible and never inventing claims — then run the project's consistency checks (citations, cross-references).
Writing-for-agents applied directly: the same pointer/load/leading-word/pruning theory governs authoring prompts, agent memory files, and vault conventions for knowledge-work agents.
